# 1 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_013_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Simon heard that Trypho had assembled a great army to come into the land of Judah and destroy it.

**2** And he saw that the people were in fear and trembling, and he went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people together

**3** and encouraged them and said to them: "You know yourselves all that I and my brothers and my father's house have done for the laws and the sanctuary, and the wars and the distresses that we have seen.

**4** For this reason all my brothers have perished for the sake of Israel, and I alone am left.

**5** And now far be it from me to spare my life in any time of tribulation, for I am not better than my brothers.

**6** But I will avenge my nation and the sanctuary and your wives and children, for all the nations have gathered to destroy us out of pure hatred."

**7** And the spirit of the people was rekindled when they heard these words,

**8** and they answered with a loud voice, saying: "You are our leader in the place of Judas and Jonathan your brothers.

**9** Fight our battle, and all that you tell us we will do."

**10** And he gathered all the men of war and hastened to finish the walls of Jerusalem and to fortify it all around.

**11** And he sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a considerable force, to Joppa; and he expelled the men from there and remained in it.

**12** And Trypho arose to come into the land with a great army, and he encamped at Adora; and Jonathan went to meet him wherever he turned.

**13** And Trypho encamped against Baskama and Trypho encamped against it.

**14** And Trypho saw that Jonathan had fallen into his power, and he sent to Simon his brother saying:

**15** "For the hundred talents of silver that your brother Jonathan owed to the royal treasury on account of the offices which he held, and for the two sons he left behind with us as hostages, we are holding him.

**16** And now send a hundred talents of silver and his two sons and we will release him; for if we do not, we will not release him."

**17** And Simon knew that they spoke to him with deceit, yet he ordered the money and the children to be sent, lest he incur great hostility among the people,

**18** who might say: "Because he did not send him the money and the children he perished."

**19** And he sent the children and the hundred talents, and he deceived and did not release Jonathan.

**20** And after this Trypho came into the land to destroy it and went around by the road to Adora; and Simon and his army kept opposite him to every place wherever he turned.

**21** And those in the citadel sent to Trypho to hasten to come to them through the wilderness and to send them provisions.

**22** And Trypho got all his cavalry ready to go, but that night there was a very heavy snow, and he did not come because of the snow, and he arose and went into Gilead.

**23** And when he came near Baskama, he killed Jonathan and he was buried there.

**24** And Trypho turned and went back to his own land.

**25** And Simon sent and took the bones of Jonathan his brother and buried him at Modein the city of his fathers.

**26** And all Israel made great lamentation for him and mourned him for many days.

**27** And Simon built a monument over the tomb of his father and his brothers and raised it high with polished stone on the back and the front.

**28** And he set up seven pyramids, one against another, for his father and his mother and his four brothers.

**29** And for the pyramids he made large columns and upon the columns armor for a perpetual memorial, and beside the armor carved ships, so that they might be seen by all who sail the sea.

**30** This is the tomb he made at Modein, and it stands to this day.

**31** Now Trypho dealt treacherously with the young King Antiochus and killed him

**32** and reigned in his place and put on the crown of Asia and brought great evil upon the land.

**33** And Simon built the strongholds of Judea and walled them with high towers and great walls and gates and bars, and laid up food in the strongholds.

**34** And Simon chose men and sent to King Demetrius to grant remission to the country, for all that Trypho was doing was plunder.

**35** And King Demetrius sent him a letter in response to these things, in these words:

**36** "King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and Friend of Kings and to the elders and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**37** The golden crown and the palm branch which you sent, we have accepted, and we are ready to make a complete peace with you and to write to the officials to grant you the remissions.

**38** And whatever we have confirmed to you, it remains firm, and the strongholds which you have built shall be yours.

**39** And we pardon any errors and offenses committed up to this day, and the crown tax which you owe, and whatever other tax was collected in Jerusalem, no longer shall any of them be collected from henceforth.

**40** And if any of you are qualified to be enrolled among the king's men, let them be enrolled; and let there be peace between us."

**41** In the one hundred and seventieth year the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel,

**42** and the people began to write on their records and contracts: "In the first year of Simon, the great high priest and commander and leader of the Jews."

**43** In those days he encamped against Gazara and went around it with troops; and he made an engine and brought it against the city and struck a tower and took it.

**44** And those in the engine leaped out into the city, and a great tumult arose in the city.

**45** And those in the city went up on the wall with their wives and children and tore their clothes and cried out with a great voice, requesting Simon to give them his right hand;

**46** and they said: "Do not deal with us according to our wickedness but according to your mercy."

**47** And Simon was reconciled to them and stopped fighting against them, and he expelled them from the city and purified the houses in which there were idols, and then he entered it with hymns and blessings.

**48** And he removed from it all uncleanness and settled in it men who observed the law, and he strengthened it and made a dwelling for himself in it.

**49** And those in the citadel at Jerusalem were not allowed to go out or to go into the country or to buy or to sell; and they were very hungry, and many of them died of famine.

**50** And they cried out to Simon to receive their right hand, and he gave it to them; and he expelled them from there and cleansed the citadel from its pollutions.

**51** And he entered it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches and with harps and with cymbals and with lutes, and with hymns and with songs, because a great enemy had been trampled down from Israel.

**52** And he appointed it to be observed every year with joy and gladness. And he strengthened the hill of the temple which is beside the citadel and he and those with him dwelt there.

**53** And Simon saw that John his son was grown up to be a man, and he made him commander of all the forces; and he dwelt in Gazara.
